Aetna Member Appeals

Re: Appeal of Medical-Necessity Denial  
Member: Jordan Jennings  
Member ID: W990598603  
Plan: Aetna Commercial/ACA — Pennsylvania  
Reference number: POC-3F7F71F65B-18736  
Requested service: Bunion surgery, CPT 28296  
Date of denial notice: August 8, 2026

Dear Aetna Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal Aetna’s denial of prior authorization for CPT 28296. The denial states that the submitted imaging findings do not support medical necessity. The submitted and enclosed records demonstrate that the imaging meets Aetna’s published criteria for bony-correction bunionectomy and that the clinical requirements are also substantially supported.

Aetna’s publicly available Medical Clinical Policy Bulletin, Bunionectomy, CPB 0629, states:

“Radiographic confirmation ... of the most recent weight-bearing view X-ray demonstrating both of the following: An HVA of 30 degrees or greater; and An inter-metatarsal angle (IMA) ... of 12 degrees or greater.”

The June 23, 2026 weight-bearing foot radiographs document:

- Hallux valgus angle: 38 degrees
- Intermetatarsal angle: 17 degrees

These measurements exceed the policy thresholds of 30 degrees for the hallux valgus angle and 12 degrees for the intermetatarsal angle. The radiographs were weight-bearing studies, and the radiology report is enclosed.

The policy also states:

“Radiographic confirmation must include interpretation and report of weight bearing anterior/ posterior and lateral views of the affected foot.”

The enclosed June 23, 2026 imaging report should be reviewed to confirm the documented views and interpretation. If Aetna believes that any required view or report component is missing, please identify the specific missing item and provide the applicable criterion used in this review.

The clinical records also support medical necessity. The policy states:

“The member's pain and symptoms over the medial bony eminence or calluses persist, making walking difficult despite at least a 6-month trial of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional.”

Jordan has experienced 14 months of progressive foot pain that has not been relieved by rest. Jordan cannot tolerate closed shoes, has ulceration risk over the prominence, and has limited range of motion because of pain. Examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side.

The records document the following conservative measures:

- NSAID treatment for 8 months, with inadequate relief;
- Corticosteroid injection on April 14, 2026, producing only 4 weeks of partial relief;
- Activity modification;
- Wide-toe-box footwear;
- Custom orthotic treatment;
- Structured conservative treatment documented in the physical therapy discharge note from March 21, 2026 through June 27, 2026, with 24 visits completed.

The policy identifies the following conservative measures:

“Protective cushions/pads; Shoe inserts ...; Corticosteroid injections; Debridement of hyperkeratotic lesions; Oral analgesics or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs); [and] Alternative or modified footwear ...”

The records therefore document multiple policy-listed conservative treatments, including shoe inserts, corticosteroid injection, oral NSAIDs, and alternative footwear, along with activity modification and prolonged symptoms despite treatment.

The policy further states that the member must have one or more qualifying clinical findings, including:

“limited or painful range of motion at the first toe MTP joint”

Jordan’s examination documents range of motion limited by pain. This criterion is therefore supported by the enclosed examination record.

Please conduct a complete reconsideration of the denial, including review of the actual June 23, 2026 weight-bearing radiographs and their report, rather than relying only on a summary of the submitted imaging. Please also consider the full conservative-treatment history and the examination findings.

If Aetna maintains the denial, please provide:

1. The specific imaging finding that Aetna contends fails to meet the applicable criterion;
2. The exact policy version and any additional clinical-review criteria applied to this request;
3. The clinical reviewer’s explanation for rejecting the documented HVA of 38 degrees and IMA of 17 degrees;
4. A complete copy of the records and criteria relied upon in making the determination; and
5. Instructions for any further internal or external review available under the plan.

Please reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 28296. The requested procedure is supported by the documented deformity, significant functional limitation, persistent pain despite conservative treatment, painful restricted motion, and weight-bearing radiographs showing hallux valgus and intermetatarsal angles above the thresholds stated in Aetna’s published policy.

Sincerely,

Jordan Jennings
